what_its_for: Meloxicam is used to relieve pain, swelling, and stiffness caused by arthritis (including osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis). It belongs to a group of medicines called NSAIDs (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs), which work by reducing substances in your body that cause pain and inflammation.
how_to_take: Take meloxicam by mouth exactly as your doctor prescribed. You can take it with or without food, but taking it with food or milk may help prevent stomach upset. Swallow tablets whole with a full glass of water. If you have the orally disintegrating tablet (ODT), place it on your tongue and let it dissolve — do not chew or swallow it whole. Always use the lowest dose that controls your symptoms, for the shortest time possible.
dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is 7.5 mg once daily. Your doctor may increase your dose to 15 mg once daily if needed. Do not take more than 15 mg in one day. For children (2 years and older), the dose is based on body weight and will be determined by your doctor. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next scheduled dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store meloxicam at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medication safely — ask your pharmacist about a drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking meloxicam, as it increases your risk of stomach bleeding. Do not take other NSAIDs (like ibuprofen or naproxen) at the same time unless your doctor tells you to. Avoid aspirin unless your doctor specifically directs you to use it. Limit sun exposure and use sunscreen, as meloxicam may make your skin more sensitive to sunlight. Avoid taking meloxicam if you are allergic to aspirin or other NSAIDs.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: chest pain, shortness of breath, weakness, or slurred speech (signs of heart attack or stroke); black, tarry, or bloody stools; vomiting blood or material that looks like coffee grounds (signs of stomach bleeding); severe stomach pain; yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice); dark urine or unusual tiredness (liver problems); swelling of your face, lips, throat, or tongue (allergic reaction); decreased urination or unusual swelling in your legs or ankles (kidney problems); or a severe skin rash or blistering.
when_it_works: Many people start to feel some pain relief within a few hours of taking the first dose. However, for full anti-inflammatory effects and the best relief of arthritis symptoms, it may take up to 2 weeks of regular use. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor, even if you feel better.
special_populations: Older adults (65+): Use with extra caution. You may be at higher risk for stomach bleeding, kidney problems, and heart issues. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose. Pregnancy: Do NOT use meloxicam at 20 weeks of pregnancy or later unless absolutely necessary, as it can harm the unborn baby. Avoid it entirely during the last 3 months (third trimester). Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using meloxicam while breastfeeding. Kidney or liver disease: Use with caution. Your doctor may need to adjust your dose or monitor you more closely. Children under 2 years: Not recommended.
